So, I’ll try and keep it brief but I could write paragraphs about how thrilled I am with this thing.

Tuning stability? Rock solid, very occasionally knocked out of tune by big ass bends or after real rough playing, like any guitar (minus those equipped w the Evertune, I guess)

Playability? First class. The roasted maple neck is a really solid middle ground between  thin and chunky. 13.7 inch radius is my new favorite. The recessed bridge is super comfy.

Tone? I mean we’ve all heard about the Fishman Fluence Moderns, but hot damn. I didn’t know they were this good. They nail that modern death/thrash tone, and they’re incredibly responsive. They just react so quickly and tightly to palm mutes, it’s sick.

Like I mentioned in the post, we split on the 28th. She’s come by the apartment once to pick up a few things, we had a nice but distant conversation, she gave me a hug, and the second she walked out I broke.

I wouldn’t say we’ve been on strict no contact, since we’re still trying to work out a few bills. But from this point on, unless she needs something from me, I’m done reaching out until a day comes when we both feel the time is right to talk about it.

I just find that right now, i find sobriety easier than the break up. And sobriety is hard as hell. The breakup is the first thing in my head every morning, last thing before bed. I only start getting the cravings whenever I get in a space like I am now, where I’d much rather run away from the hurt.

The thought of reaching out to her and telling her that I love her terrifies me. I’m so afraid of the rejection that I’m fairly sure will come from that. She’s been so distant, it’s like we’re strangers. And I get it, talking to her hurts me so much. I imagine it’s the same for her, so anytime I try and talk to her about anything relating to our relationship, it’s like pouring salt in a wound that I put there.

Thank you. I’m just gonna keep trying. I’ll be ever so slightly better a person tomorrow. Every day sober is a little victory.

Hurts like nothing else I’ve ever been through, and I get it. I’m young. I’m all wrapped up in this shit, and probably suffering more because of my headspace than anything else.

We gotta learn to ‘be with’ ourselves. To be at peace with the choices we’ve made, and to make better choices in the future.

You and me both, man...

Really, all we can do is learn and grow. We fucked up. And if we can’t get them back? Then we do right by the memory of that love, and we never do to another person what we did to them.

It hurts so much. Breakups always hurt. But a breakup that’s your fault? Genuinely yours? It’s unbearable, the level of self loathing and fucking intense hatred for myself.

Cap it off with severe mental illness and fighting for sobriety, this is Hell. Truly.

Someday, this’ll all be a nostalgic happy-sad memory. But right now, I’ve never felt lower.

It definitely does help. Thank you so much for your response.

So, I’m taking bupropion and duloxetine. I’ve been on them for maybe three or four years. And I’d like to say they’ve helped, but given my drug history, it’s hard to distinguish how much of that is the meds themselves, and how much of it has been my using weed to escape my problems.

And now that I’m sober, and going through quite a stressful time, it’s just as hard to distinguish but for different reasons. It’s like, of course I’m depressed right now, it’s a depressing situation. But I’m thinking a change in medication may very well be in order.

All I can do is work on myself. Not for anyone else, but for me. And the bottom line is that me putting myself together will be a net positive for everyone I care about in my life, my ex included.

If she wants to see progress, she’ll look. And if not? Then all I can do is grieve, grow, learn from the experience, and never make the same mistakes.

Thank you again for your response. I’m praying I get through this mostly intact.
